cases.citation: plutiedev dma-transfer (source and length are measured in words; VRAM DMA command 0x40000080; the VDP copies the ROM data to video memory); the ROM table's word 0 is 0x01c0 by construction (dma.s)
plutiedev dma-transfer (length in words; the destination advances by the register 15 auto-increment); table word 32 is 0x21e0 by construction, so it lands at VRAM 0x2040
plutiedev dma-transfer (a length of 64 words transfers words 0..63); table word 63 is 0x40ff by construction, so it lands at VRAM 0x207e
plutiedev dma-transfer (the length register bounds the transfer): the sentinel 0x5a5a written to VRAM 0x2080 before the transfer is not overwritten by a 64-word transfer ending at 0x207f

The 68000 is held while the VDP transfers (Sega documentation); how far the HV counter advances during the 64-word transfer depends on the unmeasured slot schedule and Genewhip's instruction timing. Observed HV words (before, after) are reported only; the halt duration is checked as Genewhip model conformance in vdp_timing_contract
plutiedev dma-transfer (CRAM DMA command 0xC0000080, source and length in words) and vdp-commands (CRAM read 0x00000020); the first of four ROM words, 0x0e4a, lands at CRAM address 8
plutiedev dma-transfer (length of 4 words transfers words 0..3); the fourth ROM word, 0x0888, lands at CRAM address 14
plutiedev dma-transfer (VSRAM DMA command 0x40000090) and vdp-commands (VSRAM read 0x00000010); the first of three ROM words, 0x0123, lands at VSRAM address 2
plutiedev dma-transfer (length of 3 words transfers words 0..2); the third ROM word, 0x0155, lands at VSRAM address 6

plutiedev dma-transfer documents only that a source must not cross a 128KB boundary; the data a crossing transfer reads (the low 16 bits of the word source increment and wrap inside the 128 KiB block) is commonly reported hardware behaviour not independently re-read for this plan, so it is labelled REF-derived and is not counted as documented hardware evidence. Source 0xFFFFFC, four words: 0x3333, 0x4444, then the block start (work RAM 0xFF0000: 0x1111, 0x2222)

plutiedev vdp-registers (register 23 DMD 10 = VRAM fill, registers 19/20 length) and vdp-commands (the fill starts with the data-port write after the DMA command); a 64-byte fill from VRAM 0x3010 with trigger word 0xaaaa and auto-increment 1 leaves words 0x3014 and 0x3040, deep inside the range, as 0xaaaa
plutiedev vdp-registers (registers 19/20 give the fill length in bytes): the sentinel 0x0000 written to VRAM 0x3060 is 16 bytes past the end of the 64-byte range and stays untouched
Sega documentation status register bit 1 (DMA busy) while a fill runs; a 64-byte fill takes far longer than the one instruction between the trigger and this status read
Sega documentation status register bit 1 (DMA busy) reads clear after polling until it clears
How the trigger word and the first filled byte share VRAM 0x3010, and the byte lane of the first fill byte, are not independently sourced; observed word reported only
Whether the last filled byte lands at 0x3050 or one byte earlier or later depends on the unsourced trigger/length convention; observed word reported only
Sega documentation status register bit 1 (DMA busy) while a VRAM copy runs; a 16-byte copy takes far longer than the one instruction between the command and this status read
Sega documentation status register bit 1 (DMA busy) reads clear after polling until it clears

plutiedev vdp-registers (register 23 DMD 11 = VRAM copy, registers 21/22 the VRAM source, 19/20 the length in bytes, destination from the command): 16 bytes from VRAM 0x2000 are duplicated at 0x3100, so the word at 0x3100 equals ROM table word 0
plutiedev vdp-registers (VRAM copy duplicates the source byte range in order, destination stepping by the register 15 auto-increment 1): the word at 0x3108 equals table word 4
plutiedev vdp-registers (a copy of 16 bytes covers source bytes 0x2000..0x200f): the word at 0x310e equals table word 7

The meaning of a DMA length of 0 (no transfer or 65536 units) is not independently sourced here (assumption A10); Genewhip transfers nothing, and the observed VRAM word after the command is reported only
Which byte of the trigger word fills the range and how replication behaves with distinct bytes (0xab12) are not independently sourced; observed words at 0x3300 and 0x3302 reported only

What the VDP does with a CPU data-port write while a fill is running is not independently sourced; Genewhip holds the CPU until the fill finishes and then performs the write; observed word at 0x3500 reported only
ROM control flow reached the final store (no stop before the last read-back)
